items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: A finite observational experiment with a categorical confounder. One unit is the triple \(O=(X,A,Y)\) taking values in \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\), where \([d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}\) with \(d\ge 2\), \(A\) is a binary treatment and \(Y\) a binary outcome. An observed law \(\mathbb P\) is described by its atom masses \(q_{ay,x}=\mathbb P(X=x,A=a,Y=y)\), collected into the four-vector \(q_x=(q_{00,x},q_{01,x},q_{10,x},q_{11,x})\) and the table \(\mathbf q=(q_x)_{x=1}^d\); these determine the cell mass \(p_x=\mathbb P(X=x)\), the propensity \(\pi_x=\mathbb P(A=1\mid X=x)\) and the outcome regressions \(\mu_{ax}=E_{\mathbb P}[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) on occupied cells. For a fixed overlap constant \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is the class of such laws whose occupied cells satisfy \(\epsilon\le\pi_x\le 1-\epsilon\); the cell masses are otherwise unrestricted and null cells are allowed. The sampling model is \(n\) independent observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) with common law \(\mathbb P\), indexed by \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). The estimation target is \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=\sum_{x=1}^d p_x\max_{a}\mu_{ax}\), the loss is squared error, and \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) is the infimum over all measurable estimators of the worst-case risk over \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). The rate scale is \(L_d=\log(ed)\), and \(c_\epsilon,C_\epsilon\) denote the two constants of the frontier. — Encoding: `Obs d := Fin d × Bool × Bool`, `structure DiscreteLaw (d) where pmf : PMF (Obs d)`, `obsLaw P := P.pmf.toMeasure`, `productLaw P n := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin n => obsLaw P)`. Risk uses `Causalean.Stat.sqRisk` (Causalean/Stat/Minimax/MinimaxRisk.lean:180) and the minimax value uses `Causalean.Stat.minimaxValue` (Causalean/Stat/Minimax/MinimaxValue.lean:59) at `E = {f : (Fin n → Obs d) → ℝ // Measurable f}`, `Θ = the class subtype`. WORLD-CHOICE SEARCH TRACE: surveyed `Causalean/Estimation/MinimaxATE/Model.lean` (`ValidDGP`, `obsLaw`, `minimaxMiss`) — bypass-justified: that world fixes a uniform covariate marginal and indexes the class by nuisance-estimator quality `(mhat, ghat, εg, εm)`, whereas this note needs arbitrary/null cell masses and a class indexed only by overlap; surveyed `Causalean/Estimation/Efficiency/`, `Causalean/Stat/Nonparametric/` — different (semiparametric/smooth) abstraction. ANALOGOUS MODULE (same world, same four-cell overlap cone, different estimand): `CausalSmith/Stat/STAT_DiscreteAteMinimaxLoggap_Research/Basic.lean:26-198` (`Obs`, `DiscreteLaw`, `jointMass`, `cellVector`, `cellMass`, `armMass`, `propensity`, `outcomeMean`, `Overlap`, `productLaw`, `mse`, `minimaxRisk`) — F2 should mirror that encoding verbatim; it is a sibling CausalSmith run, not an importable curated dependency (no CausalSmith run imports another run's modules), so the definitions are re-declared locally in this run's `Basic.lean`.

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl: A finite binary potential-outcome overlay on the same alphabet. A full-data law \(P\) is a law of \((X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\) with \(X\in[d]\) and \(A,Y,Y(0),Y(1)\in\{0,1\}\). Its observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\) is the law of \((X,A,Y)\). Under consistency \(Y=Y(A)\) and armwise conditional exchangeability \(Y(a)\perp A\mid X\), \(P\) carries the causal optimal-treatment value \(V^\star(P)=E_P[\max_{a}E_P\{Y(a)\mid X\}]\). The causal completion class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) collects the full-data laws satisfying both causal conditions whose observed margin lies in the overlap class of \(\mathrm{S1}\). — Encoding: `FullObs d := Fin d × Bool × Bool × Bool × Bool`, `structure PotentialLaw (d) where pmf : PMF (FullObs d)`, `observedMarginal Q := ⟨Q.pmf.map (fun z => (z.1, z.2.1, z.2.2.1))⟩`. SEARCH TRACE: grepped `Causalean/PO/` for `Consistency`, `CondIndepCF`, `POSystem`, `POVar` — found `Causalean.PO.Consistency` (Causalean/PO/Assumptions/Consistency.lean:53), `Causalean.PO.POSystem.CondIndepCF` (Causalean/PO/Assumptions/IndepCF.lean:105), `Causalean.PO.Assumptions.ConsistencyLemmas.*`. BYPASS-JUSTIFIED: those are regime-indexed measure-theoretic potential-outcome systems over an abstract `P.Ω` with counterfactual variables and `EventCondExp` conditioning; here every variable is a coordinate of a five-fold finite Bool/Fin product and the whole identification argument is finite summation over atoms, so the regime-indexed API is a strictly different abstraction level and would add a measure-theoretic layer with no mathematical content. The same bypass was taken and accepted in the sibling four-cell run (`CausalSmith/Stat/STAT_DiscreteAteMinimaxLoggap_Research/Basic.lean:1-10, 204-241`), which is the ANALOGOUS MODULE for `PotentialLaw`, `Consistency`, `ConditionalExchangeability`, `poAtom`, `observedMarginal`.

items.label: Setup S-3
items.nl: The four-cell analytic cone and the Poissonized pilot/evaluation construction. Write \(\mathcal J=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}\) with generic coordinate \(\jmath\), and for \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\) put \(s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1}\) and \(s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u)\). The overlap cone is \(\mathcal C_\epsilon=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^4:\epsilon s(u)\le s_1(u)\le(1-\epsilon)s(u)\}\), and \(\bar f_\epsilon\) is a globally Lipschitz extension to all of \(\mathbb R_+^4\) of the cell contribution to the target. Fixed universal numerical constants \(H_0>0\), \(0<\kappa<1\) and a cutoff \(D_0\in\mathbb N\) calibrate the Jackson degree \(K_d=\max\{2,\lfloor\kappa L_d\rfloor\}\) and the one-dimensional order-four Jackson kernel \(J_{K_d}\). An auxiliary count \(M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\) and independent fair marks \(B_i\in\{0,1\}\) split the included observations into pilot counts \(N'_{\jmath,x}\) and evaluation counts \(N_{\jmath,x}\). The pilot builds a random rectangle \(Q_x\subseteq\mathbb R_+^4\), the kernel builds the tensor polynomial \(P_{x,K_d}\) on \(Q_x\), the centered factorial operator \(U_h(N;z)\) lifts monomials to unbiased statistics of the evaluation counts, and clipping produces the cell estimator \(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}\). Summing, projecting to \([0,1]\) and Rao--Blackwellizing gives \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\), which falls back to the empirical-ratio statistic \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\) on bounded alphabets. \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{const}}\) names the (open) sharp-constant derivation route attached to this construction. — Encoding: `Cell := Fin 2 × Fin 2` (so \(\mathcal J\) is `Cell` and \(\jmath\) ranges over it), \(u\) is `Cell → ℝ`, \(Q_x\) is a pair of endpoint functions `Cell → ℝ`, \(P_{x,K_d}\) is `MvPolynomial Cell ℝ`, \(U_h(N;z)\) is a `ℕ → ℝ → ℝ` built from `Nat.descFactorial`. SEARCH TRACE (Causalean CLI concept words: `Jackson kernel`, `Fejer kernel`, `trigonometric polynomial approximation`, `positive kernel convolution`, `factorial moment unbiased estimator`, `Poisson splitting marks pilot`): Causalean HAS the marked-Poisson layer — `Causalean.Mathlib.Probability.FiniteMarkedPoissonPartition.finiteMarkedPoissonSampleLaw`, `.map_restrictPartition_finiteMarkedPoissonSampleLaw`, `.finitePoissonSampleLaw_map_count` — which supplies the Poisson-splitting independence of \((N'_{\jmath,x},N_{\jmath,x})\) across cells; and the even-trig-polynomial layer — `Causalean.Mathlib.Analysis.BernsteinSzegoTrig.IsTrigPolyLE`, `.cosComp_isTrigPolyLE`, `.cos_nat_mul_isTrigPolyLE` — which supplies the `even trigonometric polynomial of degree D ↔ polynomial of degree D in cos` bridge that `def:jackson-kernel` needs. Causalean does NOT contain a Jackson/Fejér kernel: `Causalean/Stat/Nonparametric/SeriesSieve/Jackson.lean` despite its filename contains only `piecewiseTaylorApprox` / `piecewiseTaylor_sup_approx_rate` (piecewise Taylor sieve, not the Jackson convolution kernel) — that is a filename false positive, confirmed by reading its declarations. MATHLIB-SIDE CHECK: `lean_leansearch "Jackson kernel trigonometric polynomial approximation modulus of continuity"` returned only `ContinuousMap.modulus`, `bernsteinApproximation`, `exists_polynomial_near_of_continuousOn` — no Jackson/Fejér kernel and no quantitative degree-\(K\) rate; `lean_loogle "Polynomial.Chebyshev.T"` confirms the Chebyshev basis (`Polynomial.Chebyshev.T`, `T_mul`, `T_real_cos`) is available for the coefficient-envelope half. So the kernel itself is new local construction over reused trig-polynomial and Poisson substrate.

items.label: Setup S-4
items.nl:
The Poissonized moment-matching lower-bound experiment. \(\Delta_d=\{R\in\mathbb R_+^d:\sum_x R_x=1\}\) is the probability simplex, and \(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q\in\Delta_d\) are the two multinomial laws of the normalized two-sample distance experiment. The dense hard submodel is indexed by a contrast vector \(	heta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\) through the equal-mass law \(P_	heta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) with \(p_x=1/d\), \(\pi_x=1/2\) and \(\mu_{1x}=(1+	heta_x)/2\), \(\mu_{0x}=(1-	heta_x)/2\). For an even degree \(K\), \(E_K=\inf_{\deg p\le K}\sup_{|t|\le1} igl||t|-p(t) igr|\) is the best even-polynomial approximation error of the absolute value, and \(
u_{0,K},
u_{1,K}\) are symmetric probability measures on \([-1,1]\) whose moments agree through degree \(K\) with absolute-moment gap \(2E_K\). Setting \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil 4L_dceil\), \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\) and \(a_{n,d}=\sqrt{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}/(64\lambda_{n,d})}\), the scaled product priors \(\Pi_{0,n,d},\Pi_{1,n,d}\) on \([-a_{n,d},a_{n,d}]^d\) induce the two observation mixtures \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d},\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\) when the total sample size is an independent \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\). Here \(r\) indexes the exponential likelihood expansion, \(L_{	heta_x}\) is the one-cell Poisson likelihood ratio against \(	heta_x=0\), \(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}\) is the separation of the two prior means of the target, and \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}\) is the minimax squared risk in that Poissonized experiment. — SEARCH TRACE (concept words: `two point lower bound squared loss`, `total variation testing error`, `chi square tensorization product`, `Poisson depoissonization fixed sample transfer`, `fuzzy hypotheses mixture prior`): Causalean HAS the whole lower-bound plumbing — `Causalean.Stat.tvDist` and `Causalean.Stat.one_sub_tvDist_le_test` (Minimax/TotalVariation.lean:49,107), `Causalean.Stat.half_one_sub_tvDist_le_max_error` (Minimax/LeCam.lean:76), `Causalean.Stat.two_point_lower_bound_of_tvDist_le` / `two_point_lower_bound_of_chiSqDiv_le` / `iid_two_point_lower_bound` (Minimax/MinimaxRisk.lean:74,105,88), `Causalean.Stat.chiSqDiv_prod` and `one_add_chiSqDiv_pi_iid_general` (Minimax/ChiSquared.lean:184,419), and `Causalean.Mathlib.Probability.FiniteMarkedPoissonPartition.poisson_two_n_lower_tail` + `map_canonicalPrefixObservations_restrict_count_ge` (Depoissonization.lean:198,163), which is exactly the `apply a fixed-n estimator to the first n observations of a Pois(2n) sample` transfer used at the end of `lem:dense-moment-matching-lower` and in `thm:all-estimator-lower`. Causalean does NOT contain the moment-matched pair \((
u_{0,K},
u_{1,K})\) for \(|t|\) nor the value of \(E_K\): grepped `Chebyshev|bestApprox|moment matching prior|Bernstein constant` across `Causalean/` — the closest hits are `Causalean/Mathlib/Analysis/BernsteinSzegoTrig/*` (Bernstein--Szegő derivative inequalities, not best approximation of \(|t|\)) and `Causalean/Stat/Nonparametric/MomentProblems/*` (score/residual moment programs). MATHLIB-SIDE CHECK: `lean_loogle "Polynomial.Chebyshev.T"` and `lean_leansearch` for best uniform approximation of the absolute value return nothing quantitative. That absence is precisely the frozen cited gate `lem:cai-low-absolute-moment-priors`.

items.label: Definition P-1
items.nl: \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}:=\{P:P\text{ is a law of }(X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\text{ with }X\in[d],\ A,Y,Y(0),Y(1)\in\{0,1\},\ P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency}\text{ and }\mathrm{ass:conditional-exchangeability},\text{ and }\operatorname{Obs}(P)\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\}\) for every \(d\geq2\) and \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).

items.label: Definition P-2
items.nl: \(\mathcal C_\epsilon:=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^4:\epsilon s(u)\leq s_1(u)\leq(1-\epsilon)s(u)\}\), where \(s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1}\) and \(s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u)\).

items.label: Definition P-3
items.nl: For \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\) with \(s(u)>0\), define \(g_{a,\epsilon}(u):=s(u)u_{a1}/\max\{s_a(u),\epsilon s(u)\}\) and \(\bar f_\epsilon(u):=\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}g_{a,\epsilon}(u)\); set \(g_{a,\epsilon}(0)=\bar f_\epsilon(0)=0\).

items.label: Definition P-4
items.nl: \(V^\star(P):=E_P[\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}E_P\{Y(a)\mid X\}]\).  This is a full-data causal functional; its equality to an observed-law functional is asserted only by \(\mathrm{prop:causal-optimal-value-corollary}\).

items.label: Definition P-5
items.nl: Let \(\overline N_x=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}\), \(\overline N_{ax}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a\}\), and \(\overline S_{ax}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,Y_i=1\}\). Put \(\widehat p_x=\overline N_x/n\), \(\widehat\mu_{ax}=\overline S_{ax}/\overline N_{ax}\) with \(0/0=0\), and \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}=\sum_{x=1}^d\widehat p_x\max_a\widehat\mu_{ax}\).

items.label: Definition P-6
items.nl: For integer \(K_d\geq2\), let \(J_{K_d}(t)=c_{K_d}[\sin(K_dt/2)/\sin(t/2)]^4\) on \([-\pi,\pi]\), with removable values filled continuously and \(c_{K_d}\) chosen so that \(\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}J_{K_d}(t)\,dt=1\). For a rectangle \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) with center \(b_{\jmath,x}=(\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x})/2\) and radius \(r_{\jmath,x}=(u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x})/2\), define \(P_{x,K_d}\) by the even product convolution \(P_{x,K_d}(b_x+r_x\odot\cos\theta)=\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^4}\bar f_\epsilon(b_x+r_x\odot\cos(\theta+t))\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}J_{K_d}(t_{\jmath})\,dt\).

items.label: Definition P-7
items.nl: Put \(L_d=\log(ed)\), \(m=n/8\), and \(K_d=\max\{2,\lfloor\kappa L_d\rfloor\}\). If \(d<D_0\), return \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\); if \(d\geq D_0\) and \(n<d/L_d\), return \(1/2\). Otherwise draw \(M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\), and on \(M\leq n\) mark the first \(M\) observations independently by \(B_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), producing independent pilot and evaluation counts \(N'_{\jmath,x}\) and \(N_{\jmath,x}\); on \(M>n\), set the randomized output to zero. For \(M\leq n\), let \(c_{\jmath,x}=N'_{\jmath,x}/m\), \(h_{\jmath,x}=H_0\{\sqrt{c_{\jmath,x}L_d/m}+L_d/m\}\), \(\ell_{\jmath,x}=\max\{0,c_{\jmath,x}-h_{\jmath,x}\}\), \(u_{\jmath,x}=c_{\jmath,x}+h_{\jmath,x}\), and \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\), with center \(b_x\) and coordinate radii \(r_x\). Expand \(P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)=\sum_\alpha b_{x,\alpha}((v-b_x)/r_x)^\alpha\). Define \(U_h(N;z)=\sum_{t=0}^h\binom ht(-z)^{h-t}(N)_t/m^t\), \(S_x=(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath}r_{\jmath,x}\), \(Z_x=\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)+\sum_\alpha b_{x,\alpha}\prod_{\jmath}U_{\alpha_{\jmath}}(N_{\jmath,x};b_{\jmath,x})/r_{\jmath,x}^{\alpha_{\jmath}}\), and \(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}=\Pi_{[\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)-d^{1/4}S_x,\,\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)+d^{1/4}S_x]}(Z_x)\). The randomized statistic is \(\widetilde V=\Pi_{[0,1]}(\sum_xT_x^{\mathrm{JF}})\). In the Jackson branch define the all-data estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}:=E[\widetilde V\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n]\), where the conditional expectation integrates only the displayed auxiliary Poisson count and marks.

items.label: Definition P-8
items.nl: For \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), set \(q_{11,x}=q_{00,x}=P_x/4\) and \(q_{10,x}=q_{01,x}=Q_x/4\), and complete the observed law with conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes, treatment propensity \(1/2\), and consistency.

items.label: Definition P-9
items.nl: For a full-data law \(P\), define its observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\) by \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\{(x,a,y)\}=P(X=x,A=a,Y=y)\) for \((x,a,y)\in[d]\times\{0,1\}^2\).

items.label: Definition P-10
items.nl:
Let \(\Delta_d:=\{p\in[0,1]^d:\sum_{x=1}^d p_x=1\}\) be the probability simplex.  Then \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is the set of all laws \(\mathbb P\) on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\) for which there are \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_d)\in\Delta_d\), \(\pi_x\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), and \(\mu_{ax}\in[0,1]\) satisfying, for every \(x\in[d]\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 q_{a1,x}=p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}\mu_{ax},\qquad
 q_{a0,x}=p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}(1-\mu_{ax}),
\]
where \(q_{ay,x}=\mathbb P(X=x,A=a,Y=y)\), and write \(q_x=(q_{00,x},q_{01,x},q_{10,x},q_{11,x})\) for the resulting four-vector in cell \(x\).  Thus the support contains at most \(d\) covariate cells; the parameters on a null cell may be chosen arbitrarily within their displayed ranges.

items.label: Definition P-11
items.nl: For \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) with table \(\mathbf q=(q_x)_{x=1}^d\), define the observed-law optimal-regression functional by \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=\Psi(\mathbf q):=\sum_{x=1}^d p_x\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\mu_{ax}\).  This value is independent of the permitted choice of \(\mu_{ax}\) on cells with \(p_x=0\).

items.label: Definition P-13
items.nl:
For \(	heta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\), define \(P_	heta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) by \(p_x=1/d\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), \(\mu_{1x}=(1+	heta_x)/2\), and \(\mu_{0x}=(1-	heta_x)/2\). Complete the observed law by drawing \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, drawing \(A\mid X=x\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of the potential outcomes, and setting \(Y=Y(A)\). For even \(K\), let \(E_K=\inf_{p:\deg(p)\leq K}\sup_{t\in[-1,1]}\lvert\lvert tvert-p(t)vert\), and obtain symmetric probability measures \(
u_{0,K}\) and \(
u_{1,K}\) by taking the negative and positive parts of twice a symmetrized norm-one Hahn--Banach measure that annihilates every polynomial of degree at most \(K\) and integrates \(\lvert tvert\) to \(E_K\). Thus their moments agree through degree \(K\) and \(\int\lvert tvert\,d
u_{1,K}-\int\lvert tvert\,d
u_{0,K}=2E_K\). Put \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil4L_dceil\), \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\), and \(a_{n,d}=\sqrt{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}/(64\lambda_{n,d})}\). Let \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) be the pushforward of \(
u_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) under the coordinatewise scaling map \(t\mapsto a_{n,d}t\), and define \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\) analogously from \(
u_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\). Let \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d}\) and \(\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\) be the respective observation mixtures when the total sample size is independent \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\). Finally, define \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}:=\inf_{\widehat V}\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}E_{\mathbb P}[(\widehat V-\Psi(\mathbb P))^2]\) in that Poissonized experiment and \(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}:=E_{\Pi_{1,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_	heta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}-E_{\Pi_{0,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_	heta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}\).

items.label: Definition P-14
items.nl: \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{const}}\) is the route that rescales the pilot-local four-cell rectangles by their Poisson noise geometry, optimizes the tensor-polynomial bias--variance functional for \(\bar f_\epsilon\), and dualizes the approximation constraint into moment-matched observed laws in \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) for the target \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\).

items.label: Definition P-15
items.nl: Along each nonsaturated sequence with \(d\to\infty\) and \(d/[n\log(ed)]\to0\), does the normalized risk \((n\log(ed)/d)\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) converge to a finite positive limit, and can an estimator attaining that limit be derived through \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{const}}\)?

items.label: Assumption A-1
items.nl: For each \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), write \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\) for the observed triple of unit \(i\).  Then \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and have common law \(\mathbb P\).

items.label: Assumption A-4
items.nl: Write \([d]:=\{1,\ldots,d\}\).  For every \(\mathbb P\) under consideration and every \(x\in[d]\) with \(p_x=\mathbb P(X=x)>0\), the conditional probability \(\pi_x=\mathbb P(A=1\mid X=x)\) satisfies \(\epsilon\leq\pi_x\leq1-\epsilon\).

items.label: Lemma lem:tensor-jackson-coefficient-envelope
items.nl: Let \(K\ge1\) be an integer, let \(f\) be continuous on the normalized cube \([-1,1]^{\mathcal J}\) indexed by the four coordinates \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\), and let \(B\ge0\) satisfy \(|f(z)|\le B\) for every \(z\in[-1,1]^{\mathcal J}\). Then there is a polynomial \(\mathcal R\) in the four normalized coordinates such that, with cosine applied coordinatewise, \(\mathcal R(\cos\varphi)=\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^{\mathcal J}}f\{\cos(\varphi-\tau)\}\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}J_K(\tau_\jmath)\,d\tau\) for every angle vector \(\varphi:\mathcal J\to\mathbb R\), where \(J_K\) is the order-four Jackson kernel; every multi-index \(\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R)\) satisfies \(\beta_\omega\le2(K-1)\) for every coordinate \(\omega\in\mathcal J\); the total degree of \(\mathcal R\) is at most \(8(K-1)\); and the coefficient one-norm obeys \(\sum_{\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R)}|\mathcal R_\beta|\le2^{40K+20}B\).

items.label: Lemma lem:jackson-tensor-extraction
items.nl: Let \(\epsilon>0\), let \(K\ge2\) be an integer, and let \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be a four-coordinate rectangle with nonnegative lower endpoints \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge0\), center coordinates \(b_{\jmath,x}\), and strictly positive radii \(r_{\jmath,x}>0\). Then there exist a polynomial \(P_{x,K}\) in the four physical coordinates and a polynomial \(\mathcal R_{x,K}\) in the four normalized coordinates such that every coordinate degree of \(P_{x,K}\) is at most \(2(K-1)\); every multi-index \(\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})\) satisfies \(\beta_\omega\le2(K-1)\) in each coordinate \(\omega\); the centered evaluation identity \(P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)=\mathcal R_{x,K}(\{(v_\jmath-b_{\jmath,x})/r_{\jmath,x}\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J})\) holds for every \(v\); for every angle vector \(\vartheta:\mathcal J\to\mathbb R\) the value \(P_{x,K}(b_x+r_x\odot\cos\vartheta)\) equals the order-\(K\) tensor Jackson convolution of \(\bar f_\epsilon\) precomposed with the affine parametrization of \(Q_x\), evaluated at \(\vartheta\); and the normalized coefficient one-norm obeys \(\sum_{\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})}|(\mathcal R_{x,K})_\beta|\le2^{40K+20}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}r_{\jmath,x}\).

items.label: Lemma lem:jackson-convolution-modulus
items.nl: Let \(K\ge1\) be an integer, let \(f\) be continuous on the normalized cube \([-1,1]^{D}\), let \(L\ge0\), and let \(a_i\ge0\) and \(b_i\ge0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,D\). Fix an angle vector \(\varphi\in\mathbb R^{D}\) and suppose that, with cosine applied coordinatewise, \(|f\{\cos(\varphi-\tau)\}-f(\cos\varphi)|\le L\sum_{i=1}^{D}\{a_i|\tau_i|+b_i\tau_i^2\}\) for every shift \(\tau\in\mathbb R^{D}\). Then the order-\(K\) tensor Jackson convolution \((\mathcal J_Kf)(\varphi)=\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^{D}}f\{\cos(\varphi-\tau)\}J_K^{\otimes D}(\tau)\,d\tau\), formed from the order-four Jackson kernel \(J_K\), satisfies \(|(\mathcal J_Kf)(\varphi)-f(\cos\varphi)|\le L\sum_{i=1}^{D}\{32a_i/K+64b_i/K^2\}\). The constants \(32/K\) and \(64/K^2\) are the first absolute moment and the second moment of \(J_K\) on \([-\pi,\pi]\), transported to the tensor kernel by its unit mass in the remaining coordinates.

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl: Let \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) have center \(b_x\) and positive radii \(r_{\jmath,x}\). The single polynomial \(P_{x,K_d}\) in \(\mathrm{def:jackson-kernel}\) has coordinate degree \(2(K_d-1)\) and satisfies, for every \(v\in Q_x\), \(\lvert P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(v)\rvert\leq C_\epsilon\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\{\sqrt{(v_{\jmath}-\ell_{\jmath,x})(u_{\jmath,x}-v_{\jmath})}/K_d+r_{\jmath,x}/K_d^2\}\). If \(P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)=\sum_\alpha b_{x,\alpha}((v-b_x)/r_x)^\alpha\), then \(\sum_\alpha\lvert b_{x,\alpha}\rvert\leq A^{K_d}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath}r_{\jmath,x}\) for a universal \(A<\infty\). Both bounds hold for the same polynomial when \(Q_x\) touches the origin, a coordinate face, or a treatment-effect tie surface.

items.label: Lemma lem:canonical-pilot-bad-moment
items.nl: Fix a Poissonized scale \(m>0\), a logarithmic level \(L\ge1\), and nonnegative coordinate intensities \(q_\jmath\), \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\). Let the four pilot counts be independent with \(N'_{\jmath,x}\sim\operatorname{Pois}(mq_\jmath)\), let \(\Gamma_x(N')=\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\lvert N'_{\jmath,x}/m-q_\jmath\rvert+H_0\{\sqrt{(N'_{\jmath,x}/m)L/m}+L/m\}]\) be the normalized aggregate pilot score with \(H_0=1024\), and let \(\mathsf G_x^c=\{\exists\jmath\in\mathcal J:\lvert N'_{\jmath,x}/m-q_\jmath\rvert>(H_0/4)\{\sqrt{(N'_{\jmath,x}/m)L/m}+L/m\}\}\) be the self-normalized bad-pilot event. Then for each power \(t\in\{1,2,4\}\), with the explicit universal constant \(C_t=10^{80(t+1)}\), \(E[\Gamma_x(N')^t\mathbf 1_{\mathsf G_x^c}]\le C_te^{-20L}\{\sqrt{(\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}q_\jmath)L/m}+L/m\}^t\).

items.label: Lemma lem:good-pilot-radius-sum
items.nl: Fix a Poissonized scale \(m>0\), an alphabet size \(d\ge1\) with \(L_d=\log(ed)\), and nonnegative coordinate intensities \(q_\jmath\ge0\) for \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\) with total mass \(p_x=\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}q_\jmath\). Let \(N'_{\jmath,x}\) be a pilot count vector, let \(c_{\jmath,x}=N'_{\jmath,x}/m\), let \(h_{\jmath,x}=H_0\{\sqrt{c_{\jmath,x}L_d/m}+L_d/m\}\) with \(H_0=1024\), and let \(Q_x\) be the canonical pilot rectangle with endpoints \(\ell_{\jmath,x}=\max\{0,c_{\jmath,x}-h_{\jmath,x}\}\) and \(u_{\jmath,x}=c_{\jmath,x}+h_{\jmath,x}\) and radii \(r_{\jmath,x}=(u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x})/2\). If the good-pilot event \(\mathsf G_x=\bigcap_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\{|c_{\jmath,x}-q_\jmath|\le h_{\jmath,x}/4\}\) holds, then the aggregate radius satisfies \(\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}r_{\jmath,x}\le2\cdot10^{6}\{\sqrt{p_xL_d/m}+L_d/m\}\), uniformly in the pilot counts and down to zero coordinate intensities.

items.label: Lemma lem:jackson-normalized-coefficient-envelope
items.nl: Let \(\epsilon>0\), let \(K\ge2\) be an integer, and let \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be a four-coordinate rectangle with \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\le u_{\jmath,x}\), \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge0\), and radii \(r_{\jmath,x}>0\), with center \(b_x\). Let \(P_{x,K}\) be the Jackson tensor polynomial attached to \(Q_x\) and let \(\{b_{x,\alpha}\}_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x}\) be the coefficients of its centered normalized expansion \(P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x}b_{x,\alpha}\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\{(v_\jmath-b_{\jmath,x})/r_{\jmath,x}\}^{\alpha_\jmath}\). Then the normalized coefficient envelope \(\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x}|b_{x,\alpha}|\le(2^{60})^{K}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}r_{\jmath,x}\) holds, and every \(\alpha\in\mathcal A_x\) satisfies \(\alpha_\jmath\le2(K-1)\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl: In the uncapped Poisson comparison experiment induced by \(M\) and \(B_i\), conditional on the pilot counts the statistics \(U_h(N;z)\) satisfy \(E[U_h(N;z)]=(q-z)^h\) and \(E[U_h(N;z)U_t(N;z)]=\sum_{\ell=0}^{h\wedge t}\binom h\ell\binom t\ell\ell!(q/m)^\ell(q-z)^{h+t-2\ell}\). With the pilot rectangles and clipping in \(\mathrm{def:jackson-factorial-estimator}\), uniformly over \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(\lvert E[T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}]-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)\rvert\leq C_\epsilon\{\sqrt{p_x/(mL_d)}+1/(mL_d)\}\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}})\leq C_\epsilon d^{1/16}\{p_xL_d/m+L_d^2/m^2\}\). The contribution of pilot failure obeys these same local \(p_x\)-dependent scales.

items.label: Lemma lem:dense-amplitude-range
items.nl: Let \(n\) and \(d\) satisfy the dense regime \(d\ge2\) and \(d^2<n\). With \(L_d=\log(ed)\), \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil4L_d\rceil\), \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\), and \(a_{n,d}=\sqrt{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}/(64\lambda_{n,d})}\) as in \(\mathrm{def:dense-moment-matching-construction}\), the dense contrast amplitude satisfies \(0<a_{n,d}\) and \(a_{n,d}\le1/2\).

items.label: Lemma L-3
items.nl:
Choose the universal cutoff \(D_0\) sufficiently large.  For every \(d\geq D_0\) and \(n>d^2\), the construction in \(\mathrm{def:dense-moment-matching-construction}\) has even degree \(8L_d\leq K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}<8L_d+2\), amplitude \(a_{n,d}^2=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}d/(128n)\leq1/4\), and, for every \(\theta\in[-a_{n,d},a_{n,d}]^d\), an observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfying \(p_x=1/d\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), \(\mu_{1x}=(1+\theta_x)/2\), \(\mu_{0x}=(1-\theta_x)/2\), and \(\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}=1/2+(2d)^{-1}\sum_{x=1}^d\lvert\theta_x\rvert\).  The symmetric measures \(\nu_{0,K}\) and \(\nu_{1,K}\) exist for every even \(K\), match moments through degree \(K\), and have absolute-moment gap \(2E_K\) with \(E_K\asymp K^{-1}\).  Consequently \(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}=a_{n,d}E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}\asymp a_{n,d}/K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\).  Writing \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\), let \(L_{\theta_x}\) denote the one-cell likelihood ratio at contrast \(\theta_x\) relative to the baseline contrast \(0\), and let \(E_0\) denote expectation under that baseline one-cell law.  Then \(E_0[L_{\theta_x}L_{\theta_x'}]=\exp(\lambda_{n,d}\theta_x\theta_x')\); hence moment matching and tensorization give
\[
\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb M_{0,n,d},\mathbb M_{1,n,d})
\leq d\left\{\sum_{r=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}+1}^{\infty}\frac{(\lambda_{n,d}a_{n,d}^2)^r}{r!}\right\}^{1/2}
\leq d\left\{\frac{(e/64)^{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}+1}}{1-e/64}\right\}^{1/2}\leq\frac1{16}.
\]
Under either product prior, \(\operatorname{Var}[\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}]\leq a_{n,d}^2/(4d)\), and \(D_0\) can be chosen so that each prior assigns probability at most \(1/8\) to a deviation of the target from its prior mean exceeding \(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}/4\).  The two fuzzy hypotheses therefore imply \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}\geq c_\epsilon(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}})^2\geq c_\epsilon d/[nK_d^{\mathrm{lb}}]\).  Finally, applying any fixed-sample estimator to the first \(n\) observations whenever an independent \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\) total count is at least \(n\) yields \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\geq\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}-P\{\operatorname{Pois}(2n)<n\}\geq c_\epsilon d/[n\log(ed)]\), after decreasing \(c_\epsilon\).

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl: For every \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), one has \(q_x\in\mathcal C_\epsilon\) and \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=\sum_{x=1}^d\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)\).  Moreover, \(0\leq\bar f_\epsilon(u)\leq s(u)\) and \(\lvert\bar f_\epsilon(u)-\bar f_\epsilon(v)\rvert\leq(1+\epsilon^{-1})\lVert u-v\rVert_1\) for all \(u,v\in\mathbb R_+^4\).  Every \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) has a completion \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) with \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)=\mathbb P\), obtained by drawing conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes with means \(\mu_{0x},\mu_{1x}\), then drawing \(A\) independently of their joint vector given \(X\), and setting \(Y=Y(A)\); conversely, \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) for every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\).

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl: For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is \(C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that the explicit all-data estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\) satisfies \(\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}E_{\mathbb P}[(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P))^2]\leq C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\) for every \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\).  The bound permits unknown unequal propensities, arbitrary occupied-cell masses, null cells, outcome means at zero or one, and exact treatment-effect ties.

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl: Every \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\) mapped by \(\mathrm{def:l1-embedding}\) has an observed margin in \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) with \(p_x=(P_x+Q_x)/2\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), and \(\Psi=1/2+\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1/4\).  From \(n\) draws from each of \(\mathbf P\) and \(\mathbf Q\), an explicit Markov kernel produces exactly \(n\) independent observations from that margin, so \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) is at least one sixteenth of the corresponding normalized two-sample \(L_1\) minimax mean-squared error.

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl: For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is \(c_\epsilon>0\) such that the observed-law minimax risk satisfies \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\geq c_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\) for every \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\).  This covers all measurable estimators over \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) by splicing the dense Poisson moment-matching subclass when \(n>d^2\), the exact normalized \(L_1\) subclass when \(d/\log(ed)\leq n\leq d^2\), and null-cell padding plus a regular two-point subclass in the saturated and bounded-alphabet regimes.

items.label: Theorem T-5
items.nl:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(0<c_\epsilon\leq C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\),
\[
c_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\leq\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\leq\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}E_{\mathbb P}[(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P))^2]
\leq C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}.
\]
Through \(\mathrm{prop:causal-optimal-value-corollary}\), the same risk frontier applies to the causal optimal-treatment value over all causal completions whose observed margins range over \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).

items.label: Theorem T-6
items.nl: The matched frontier recovers the archived downgraded predecessor as a corollary on the identical class: uniformly over \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\), the new upper rate is at most a constant multiple of \(d/n\), while its lower rate is at least a constant multiple of \(\min\{1,\sqrt d/n+d/[n\log(en)]\}\). For every \(2\leq d<D_0\), \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}=\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\). Separately, for every bounded sequence of alphabets, \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}=\Theta_\epsilon(n^{-1})\).

items.label: Theorem T-7
items.nl: Along arbitrary sequences \(n\to\infty\) with \(d=d_n\geq2\), uniform consistency for estimating \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\) over \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is possible if and only if \(d=o(n\log(en))\).  Moreover, \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}=\Theta_\epsilon(n^{-1})\) if and only if \(d=O(1)\).  By \(\mathrm{prop:causal-optimal-value-corollary}\) and observed-margin surjectivity, the same two equivalences hold for estimating \(V^\star(P)\) over \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\).

items.label: Theorem T-8
items.nl:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\), consistency and armwise conditional exchangeability imply
\[
 V^\star(P)=\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P)\}
 =\sum_{x=1}^d p_x\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\mu_{ax}.
\]
Thus the observed-law target is the unrestricted optimal-treatment value for every causal completion in \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\), while the minimax theorems themselves require only the observed law to lie in \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).

items.label: Cited result lem:cai-low-absolute-moment-priors
items.nl:
For every even integer \(K\), let \(E_K=\inf_{p:\deg(p)\leq K}\sup_{t\in[-1,1]}\lvert\lvert tvert-p(t)vert\).  There exist symmetric probability measures \(
u_{0,K}\) and \(
u_{1,K}\) on \([-1,1]\) whose moments agree through degree \(K\) and such that \(\int\lvert tvert\,d
u_{1,K}-\int\lvert tvert\,d
u_{0,K}=2E_K\).  Moreover, there are universal constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that \(c/K\leq E_K\leq C/K\).

items.label: Cited result lem:jhw-poisson-l1-lower
items.nl: There are positive universal constants such that, whenever \(d\geq2\), \(n\) is at least a constant multiple of \(d/\log(ed)\), and \(\log(en)\) is at most a constant multiple of \(\log(ed)\), the minimax mean-squared error for estimating \(\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1\) from two independent samples of respective sizes \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\), one from each of \(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q\in\Delta_d\), is bounded below by a positive constant multiple of \(\min\{1,d/[n\log(en)]\}\).
